Who is credited with discovering Germanium?
Germanium: Clemens Winkler. Germanium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ge and atomic number 32.
Bred for strength and endurance to haul heavy loads across the snow, this large sled-dog breed shares its arctic heritage with breeds like the Siberian Husky and Samoyed — what breed is it?
Alaskan Malamute is a large breed of dog that was originally bred for its strength and endurance to haul heavy freight as a sled dog.
Famed for foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry, this French mathematician was also a principal founder of the secretive Bourbaki group — who was he?
André Weil (6 May 1906 - 6 August 1998) was a French mathematician, known for his foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry.
This deciduous shrub genus in the rose family comes in black, red, and hybrid purple berry varieties, all bitter enough to usually be processed rather than eaten fresh — which genus?
Aronia is a genus of deciduous shrubs, the chokeberries, in the family Rosaceae native to eastern North America and most commonly found in wet woods and swamps.
These nocturnal blood-feeding insects from the genus Cimex can trigger skin rashes, itching, and even psychological distress from their bites — what are they commonly called?
Bed bug are insects from the genus Cimex, which are parasites that feed on blood, usually at night.
Native to North America and introduced to Europe in the 1930s, these prostrate shrubs in the genus Vaccinium range from 4 inches to 13 feet tall — what fruit is it?
Blueberry are a widely distributed and widespread group of perennial flowering plants with blue or purple berries.
Which winged insect fluttered into the fossil record around 56 million years ago and reaches adulthood only after pupating inside a chrysalis?

Butterfly are winged insects from the lepidopteran superfamily Papilionoidea, characterised by large, often brightly coloured wings that often fold together when at rest, and a conspicuous, fluttering flight.
Combining science, aesthetics, and technique, this field is the study and practice of making and using maps to communicate spatial information — what field is it?

Cartography is the study and practice of making and using maps. The fundamental objectives of traditional cartography are to:

Set the map's agenda and select traits of the object to be mapped.
Made of DNA wound around histone proteins, this substance shapes chromosomes into their distinctive forms during cell division and gatekeeps access to genes for transcription and repair — what is it?
Chromatin is a complex of DNA and protein responsible for condensing and packaging chromosomal DNA.
Known in the US as 'konk,' this sea snail's family includes so-called 'true' species identified by their long spires — what is it?
Conch is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
Unrelated to poor hygiene, this scalp condition causes flaking and mild itching and is often treated with antifungal or keratolytic remedies; about half of all adults experience it. What is it?
Dandruff is a skin condition of the scalp. It can result in social or self-esteem problems.
Native to western North America, this towering conifer is also nicknamed Oregon pine or Columbian pine, though it isn't truly a pine at all — which tree?
Douglas fir (Pseudotsuga menziesii) is an evergreen conifer species in the pine family, Pinaceae.
Tissue similar to the uterine lining grows elsewhere in the body—often on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, or pelvis—affecting roughly 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide. What is this condition?
Endometriosis is a disease in which tissue similar to the endometrium - the lining of the uterus (womb) - grows elsewhere in the body.

This suborder of meat-eating mammals groups together the 'cat-like' carnivorans — cats, hyenas, mongooses, and viverrids — in contrast to their 'dog-like' counterparts in the other major suborder. What suborder is this?
Feliformia is a suborder within the order Carnivora consisting of "cat-like" carnivorans, including cats, hyenas, mongooses, viverrids, and related taxa.
Often bonded to glucose to form table sugar, this white, water-soluble simple sugar occurs naturally in honey, tree and vine fruits, and most root vegetables — name this sugar?
Fructose is a common monosaccharide, i.e.

Found in northern South America, this tarantula is the world's heaviest and longest-bodied spider, tipping the scales at over 170 grams, though a huntsman spider still beats it on leg span — what spider is it?
Goliath birdeater (Theraphosa blondi) is a large spider that belongs to the tarantula family Theraphosidae.
This usually benign tumor made of blood vessels typically appears on a baby's skin at birth or within weeks, often on the face, scalp, chest, or back, then shrinks over childhood — what is it?
Hemangioma is a usually benign vascular tumor derived from blood vessel cell types.
Sold as a 3 percent solution for the bathroom cabinet but explosive when concentrated, this oxidizer and antiseptic carries the formula H2O2 — what is it?
Hydrogen peroxide is a chemical compound with the formula H2O2.
This flowering plant genus boasts 310 species with showy blooms, some known by the common name 'flags' and a horticultural subgroup called 'junos' — what genus is it?
Iris (plant) is a flowering plant genus of 310 accepted species with showy flowers.

A civil engineer who commanded the Australian Corps in 1918, this WWI general was called by historian A. J. P. Taylor 'the only general of creative originality produced by the First World War' — who was he?
John Monash (27 June 1865 - 8 October 1931) was an Australian military commander of the First World War and a civil engineer.

Named after a French mathematician but reportedly learned from his Swiss tutor, this calculus theorem evaluates tricky limits by taking derivatives of the numerator and denominator — what is it called?
L'Hôpital's rule (loh-pee-TAHL) is a mathematical theorem used for evaluating the limit of a quotient of two functions, each of which tends to zero or infinity, by taking each function's derivative.
This common, soft, movable, painless growth made of fatty tissue usually forms just under the skin, often on the back, shoulders, or abdomen — name this benign tumor?
Lipoma is a benign tumor made of fat tissue. The first use of the term "lipoma" to describe these tumors was in 1709.

Located partly outside the body and partly within the pelvis, this set of sex organs includes the testicles, which produce sperm to fertilize an egg during conception — which body system is being described?
Male reproductive system consists of a number of sex organs that play a role in the process of human reproduction.
A waxy crystalline compound from peppermint and corn mint, it triggers a cooling sensation and works as a mild local anesthetic to soothe a sore throat — what is it?
Menthol is a monoterpenoid organic compound that occurs naturally in the oils of certain plants in the mint family, such as corn mint and peppermint.
Classified by carbon count into trioses, pentoses, hexoses, and more, these colorless, water-soluble simple sugars are the basic building blocks of carbohydrates — what are they called?
Monosaccharide (from Greek monos: single, sacchar: sugar), also called simple sugars, are a class of organic compounds usually with the formula (CH2O)x.
Composed of a renal corpuscle and a renal tubule, this microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney numbers between 1 and 1.5 million per healthy adult kidney — name it?

Nephron is the minute or microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney. The renal corpuscle consists of a tuft of capillaries called a glomerulus and a cup-shaped structure called Bowman's capsule.
Yellowing, thickening, and a nail separating from its bed are telltale signs of this fungal infection, far more common in toenails than fingernails — what's the medical name?
Onychomycosis is a fungal infection of the nail. Onychomycosis, also known as tinea unguium, is a fungal infection of the nail.
Combining medicine with comedy, this physician organizes volunteers to clown around for orphans and patients worldwide through a nonprofit institute he founded in 1989 — who is he?
Patch Adams (born May 28, 1945) is an American physician, comedian, social activist, clown, and author.
This bird genus, part of the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae, encompasses the living flamingo species — which genus?
Phoenicopterus is a genus of birds in the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae.

First domesticated by ancient peoples of the Iranian plateau roughly 5,000 years ago, this deciduous shrub bears a fruit rich in symbolic and mythological meaning across many cultures — name the fruit?
Pomegranate (Punica granatum) is a fruit-bearing, deciduous shrub in the family Lythraceae, subfamily Punicoideae, that grows to between 1.5-5 metres (5-16 ft) tall.
Like a cosmic lighthouse, this highly magnetized, rapidly rotating neutron star is only visible from Earth when its beam of radiation sweeps directly toward us — what's the object?
Pulsar (pulsating star, on the model of quasar) is a highly magnetized rotating neutron star that emits beams of electromagnetic radiation out of its magnetic poles.

One of the rarest and most valuable precious metals, this hard, corrosion-resistant transition metal with only one naturally occurring isotope is prized for enhancing jewelry — what's the element (symbol Rh, atomic number 45)?
Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
Arising from connective tissues like bone, cartilage, muscle, and fat, this rare cancer of mesenchymal cells makes up just 1% of adult diagnoses but 15% of childhood ones. What is it?
Sarcoma is a rare type of cancer that arises from cells of mesenchymal origin.
Despite its long-nosed, mouse-like look, this small mammal is actually a closer cousin to hedgehogs and moles than to rodents — what is it?
Shrew (family Soricidae) are small mole-like mammals classified in the order Eulipotyphla.
Doctors examine the color of this coughed-up airway mucus — greenish or yellow tints can hint at infection, though not which organism caused it — what is it?
Sputum is mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways (the trachea and bronchi).
This Polish far-right entrepreneur and tax advisor placed third in the 2025 presidential election while chairing a libertarian party and co-leading a far-right coalition — who is he?
Sławomir Mentzen (born 20 November 1986) is a Polish far-right politician, entrepreneur and tax advisor.
A parasitic arachnid roughly 3 to 5 millimeters long that feeds on the blood of mammals and birds, with fossils dating back some 100 million years to the Cretaceous — which creature?
Tick are parasitic arachnids of the order Ixodida.
This broad category of large, hoofed mammals was reclassified in 2001 into a new clade after genetic data revealed the older grouping wasn't a true evolutionary lineage. Name the category of animals?
Ungulate are members of the diverse clade Euungulata, which primarily consists of large mammals with hooves.
This German hunting-dog breed, recognized in 1891, is so much a working dog that in its homeland it's considered unsuitable simply as a house pet — name the breed?
Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.
Launched in 1981 as a joint venture between French and Italian aerospace firms, this high-wing turboprop airliner later formed the basis for a stretched successor introduced in 1989 — which aircraft?
This mushroom genus of more than 400 species includes both the common button mushroom and the field mushroom, the two most-cultivated fungi in the West — which genus is it?
Approved for medical use in the US in 1966, this xanthine oxidase inhibitor lowers uric acid to prevent gout and certain kidney stones — what medication is it?
Allopurinol: Medication. Allopurinol is a medication used to decrease high blood uric acid levels.

Found along the Andes and Pacific coasts of South America, this enormous New World vulture is one of the largest flying birds by wingspan, with males sporting a fleshy comb atop a bald red head — which species is it?
Andean condor: Species of bird. The Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) is a South American New World vulture and is the only extant member of the genus Vultur.
In this severe blood disorder, the bone marrow stops producing red cells, white cells and platelets alike, and about half of all cases have no known cause — what condition is it?
Aplastic anemia: Disease causing insufficient blood cells of all types.

Often called a 'collapsed lung' in casual speech, this condition is really the partial deflation of the lung's alveoli rather than fluid filling them, and shows up frequently on chest X-rays — what is it?
Atelectasis: Partial collapse of a lung causing reduced gas exchange.
Commonly known as rays, this division of cartilaginous fish is instantly recognizable by its flattened body and enlarged pectoral fins fused to the head — what's it called?
Batomorphi: Division of cartilaginous fishes. Batomorphi, along with the shark division Selachii, both compose the subclass Elasmobranchii.
Prized for the rainbow, iridescent crust that forms when it oxidizes under heat, which brittle, silvery element is only 86 percent as dense as lead?
Bismuth: Chemical element with atomic number 83 (Bi)
This white crystalline sodium borate dissolves in water to form a basic solution and finds uses as a pesticide, a soldering flux, and an ingredient in glass and pottery glazes — what mineral is it?
Borax: Boron compound, a salt of boric acid.
This condition involves inflamed, fluid-filled sacs that normally cushion friction near joints like the shoulder, elbow, hip and knee — what is it?
Bursitis: Inflammation of the bursae (sacs of synovial fluid in joints)
Native to the Americas, this plant genus in the nightshade family produces the fruits we call peppers, including sweet bell types and fiery chilies — what genus is it?
This bacterial skin infection affects the dermis and subcutaneous fat, most often striking the legs or face and causing spreading redness and swelling — what is it?
Cellulitis: Bacterial infection of the inner layers of the skin called the dermis.
Known for a bitter metallic aftertaste that gets worse if you rinse with water, this antiseptic is used before surgery and to prevent dental plaque — what is it?
Chlorhexidine: Disinfectant and antiseptic. Chlorhexidine is a disinfectant and antiseptic which is used for skin disinfection before surgery and to disinfect surgical instruments.
This process turns blood from liquid to gel through platelet activation and fibrin formation, beginning almost instantly after a vessel is injured — what's the clotting process called?
Coagulation: Process of formation of blood clots. Coagulation, also known as clotting, is the process by which blood changes from a liquid to a gel forming a blood clot.

This physical law holds that within an isolated system, nothing is created or destroyed — only transformed, as when a stick of dynamite converts stored chemical potential into heat, sound, and motion — what law is it?
Conservation of energy: Law of physics and chemistry.
Squash, pumpkin, cucumber, watermelon, and the plant behind loofah sponges all belong to which family, nicknamed the gourds?
Cucurbitaceae: Family of plants. The Cucurbitaceae ( kew-KUR-bih-TAY-see-ee), also called cucurbits or the gourd family, are a plant family consisting of about 965 species in 101 genera.
Often tied to diseases like Alzheimer's, this incurable, progressive syndrome erodes memory, language, and motivation in stages — which condition is being described?
Sold under the brand name Motilium, this dopamine-blocking medication treats nausea and slow stomach emptying, but also raises prolactin levels — what is it?
Belonging to the order Anguilliformes and comprising roughly 1,000 species, these ray-finned predators transform dramatically from larva to adult and mostly live in salt water — what are they?
This fungal genus growing on rye and other cereals produces alkaloids that cause a poisoning condition in humans and livestock who eat contaminated grain — which group of fungi?
Ergot: Fungi of the genus Claviceps. The most prominent member of this group is Claviceps purpurea (rye ergot fungus).

Its mating has never once been observed in the wild, and its five life stages were once mistaken for five separate species — this critically endangered fish is threatened by dams and overfishing. What is it?
European eel: Species of fish. The five stages of their development were originally thought to be different species.
Once tapped as a source of natural rubber, though no longer used commercially for that purpose, this houseplant native to South and Southeast Asia is nicknamed the 'rubber tree.' Which species?
Ficus elastica: Species of banyan tree.

One of the first management consultants, this American mechanical engineer wrote a 1909 book — later voted the most influential management book of the 20th century — and helped found industrial engineering. Who was he?
Frederick Winslow Taylor: American mechanical engineer (1856–1915)
This mathematician founded set theory and proved that there are more real numbers than natural numbers, revealing an infinity of infinities — who is he?
With DNA up to 99% identical to ours, this troop-dwelling great ape — led by a dominant 'silverback' — is the largest living primate on Earth — what is it?
Gorilla: Genus of large African apes.
First described in 1893 during a flu pandemic and mistakenly blamed as its cause, this Gram-negative bacterium causes pneumonia and meningitis mainly in infants — which bacterium?
Haemophilus influenzae: Species of bacterium. The bacteria are mesophilic and grow best at temperatures between 35 and 37 °C.

Famous for the ideas of "bounded rationality" and "satisficing," this remarkable scholar won both a Turing Award and a Nobel in Economics — bridging computer science, economics, and psychology. Who was he?
Herbert A. Simon: American academic and Nobel Laureate (1916–2001)

Found only in the Americas from Alaska to Tierra del Fuego, these roughly 375 species pull off rapid, maneuverable flight thanks to an exceptional metabolism — and their males flaunt the widest plumage diversity of any bird — what are they?
Formed by the merger of two hip flexor muscles that join at the femur's lesser trochanter, this is the body's strongest flexor of the hip — what is it called?
Iliopsoas: Joined psoas and iliacus muscles of the hip and thigh.
Native to Africa and Eurasia, this opportunistic canid can sustain a running pace of about 10 mph over long distances while hunting small mammals, birds, and reptiles — which animal?
A real estate magnate and Spanish–American War officer worth roughly $87 million, he was the richest passenger aboard the Titanic — and went down with it in 1912. Who was he?
John Jacob Astor IV: American businessman and Titanic passenger (1864–1912)
This classical physics model imagines matter as countless invisible particles in constant, random collisions, explaining pressure, temperature and viscosity alike — what is it?
Kinetic theory of gases: Understanding of gas properties in terms of molecular motion.

Caused by a bacterium that thrives in fresh water and can contaminate hot tubs and water tanks, this atypical pneumonia brings cough, high fever and muscle pains days after exposure — what's it called?
Legionnaires' disease: Form of atypical pneumonia. Legionnaires' disease is a form of atypical pneumonia caused by any species of Legionella bacteria, quite often Legionella pneumophila.

A domesticated South American camelid whose Quechua name the Spanish adopted, this herd animal can haul about a quarter of its body weight for miles and learns simple tasks after a few tries — what is it?
Llama: Species of wooly domesticated mammal.
Popular as companion birds despite conservation concerns for several species, these large, long-tailed, brightly colored New World parrots belong to the tribe Arini — what are they?
Macaw: Group of birds in the parrot family.
On April 3, 1973, this Motorola engineer made history's first public call from a handheld cell phone on a Manhattan sidewalk — who is he?

From a Greek word meaning 'change,' this term covers the enzyme-driven reactions that turn food into usable energy and building blocks while excreting waste — letting organisms grow and reproduce. What is it?
Metabolism: Set of chemical reactions in organisms.
Marketed under names like Rogaine and Loniten, this medication treats high blood pressure but is best known over-the-counter for combating hair loss — what's the drug?
Minoxidil: Medication to treat high blood pressure and alopecia.
Also known as green gram, this legume is a staple ingredient across East, Southeast, and South Asian cuisine in both savory and sweet dishes — what is it?
Discovered in 1898 alongside krypton and xenon, this noble gas gets its name from the Greek word for 'new' and glows bright red in electrical discharge — what element is it?
Neon: Chemical element with atomic number 10 (Ne)
Built from nucleotide units — a sugar, a phosphate group, and a nitrogenous base — this biomolecule class includes both DNA and RNA. Which class of molecule?
Nucleic acid: Class of large biomolecules essential to all known life.

This vertebrate clade has skeletons made mostly of bone rather than cartilage, and includes both classic 'bony fish' and, cladistically, every land vertebrate descended from lobe-finned ancestors — what is it?
Osteichthyes: Diverse clade of vertebrate animals.
Known as the passion flower, this genus of about 550 species also has ornamental hybrids that have won Royal Horticultural Society awards and varieties used in ayahuasca analogs — name the genus?
Passiflora: Genus of flowering plants in the passion flower family.
What is the process by which immune cells like macrophages and neutrophils engulf pathogens and debris with their plasma membrane, forming an internal compartment called a phagosome?
Phagocytosis: Cell membrane engulfing a large particle.
Used in randomized clinical trials as a genuine-looking but pharmacologically inert stand-in — like a sugar pill or saline shot — what's this sham treatment called?
Placebo: Substance or treatment of no therapeutic value.
This rare genetic disorder linked to chromosome 15 leaves affected children constantly hungry, often leading to obesity, alongside a narrow forehead and small hands and feet — what is it?
Prader–Willi syndrome: Genetic disorder involving an imprinted genomic region.
Studied by Confucius and central to rhetoric in ancient Greece and Rome, this skill involves delivering an address to a live audience — what is it called?
Public speaking: Performing a speech to a live audience.

The largest of the true foxes and the most widely distributed carnivore on Earth, this Northern Hemisphere native is so destructive where it's been introduced that it made the list of the world's 100 worst invasive species — which animal is it?
Red fox: Species of mammal. The red fox (Vulpes vulpes) is the largest of the true foxes, and the most widely distributed member of the order Carnivora.
The wild ancestor of the domestic pigeon, this pale grey bird has two black bars on each wing and gave rise to feral pigeons worldwide — what is it?
Rock dove: Ancestor of domestic pigeon. The domestic pigeon, often called "Columba livia domestica", which includes about 1,000 different breeds, is descended from this species.
Dropped out of Stanford to co-found Loopt, later led Y Combinator, then became CEO of the company behind ChatGPT — briefly ousted by its board in 2023 for not being 'consistently candid.' Who is he?
Sam Altman: American entrepreneur and investor (born 1985)

Triggered when the body's own dysregulated response to infection starts damaging its tissues and organs, this life-threatening condition brings fever, rapid heartbeat, and confusion — which condition?

Sepsis: Life-threatening response to infection. Sepsis is a potentially life-threatening condition that arises when the body's dysregulated response to infection causes injury to its own tissues and organs.
Roughly 21 feet long yet coiled to fit inside the abdomen, this digestive tube receives bile and pancreatic juice and is divided into the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum — which organ?
Small intestine: Organ in the gastrointestinal tract.
Prized as the standard soundboard material for stringed instruments, this coniferous genus has four-sided needles and dominates boreal forests across the Northern Hemisphere — which tree genus?
Spruce: Genus of coniferous evergreen trees.
This tangy reddish spice, made from a shrub in the cashew family, is a staple of Arab cuisine and holds symbolic significance on the Haft-sin table at Persian New Year — what is it?
Sumac: Related species of plants in the family Anacardiaceae.
Prized for its durability and water resistance, this tropical hardwood with a leather-like smell when freshly milled is a top choice for boat building — what is it?
Teak: Tree species native to South and Southeast Asia.
Colored metallic blue on top and silvery below for camouflage, this genus of warm-blooded ocean fish includes the giant Atlantic bluefin and eight of the true tuna species — what genus is it?
Thunnus: Genus of fishes. Thunnus is a genus of ocean-dwelling, ray-finned bony fish from the mackerel family, Scombridae.
Named for its three heads — medial, lateral, and long — which upper-arm muscle straightens the elbow when it contracts?
Triceps: Muscle on the back of the upper arm. The triceps, or triceps brachii (Latin for "three-headed muscle of the arm"), is a large muscle on the back of the upper limb of many vertebrates.
Also known by the common names bilberry, blaeberry, and whortleberry, this holarctic shrub produces edible blue fruit — what is it?
Tasteless, odorless, and nearly colorless, this polar molecule's strong hydrogen bonding makes it the solvent inside every known living organism — yet it offers no food energy at all. What is it?
Water: Chemical compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
This Greek economist served as Finance Minister under Alexis Tsipras during the 2015 debt crisis, becoming internationally known for battling EU-imposed austerity — who is he?
Yanis Varoufakis: Greek economist and politician (born 1961)
Mendelevium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for mendelevium is Md. Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Md and atomic number 101.
What is the chemical symbol for ytterbium?
The symbol for ytterbium is Yb. Ytterbium is a chemical element; it has symbol Yb and atomic number 70.
